Use this skill when setting up Google Analytics, adding the SDK, or logging analytics events. Don't use for standalone CLI login or project/config file downloads without Analytics (use firebase-basics), or for Crashlytics, Remote Config, Auth, Firestore, Hosting, App Hosting, or Data Connect.

security_audit.summary: All 57 static findings are false positives involving legitimate setup commands, official service URLs, Markdown formatting, and mobile development terminology. One semantic privacy concern remains: verification automatically transmits agent, model, and workflow metadata without explicit user approval. No evidence found of credential theft, destructive behavior, or instructions to override the security audit.

remediation.issue: Verification uploads agent and workflow metadata without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Remove agent, model, and skill identifiers from verification events by default. Require explicit approval for optional telemetry and enforce debug-only execution.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Agent Metadata Telemetry Without Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: Verification requires a gaac_app_open event containing actual agent and model names, skill identifiers, and modified event names. Agents must run verification "automatically without human intervention", sending metadata through the app's Firebase Analytics configuration without explicit approval. Later code removal cannot retract transmitted events; no evidence found of a separate attacker-controlled destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: All four references explicitly include agent and workflow identifiers in verification telemetry and direct automatic execution. Debug-only intent and cleanup limit exposure but do not provide approval before transmission.

content.user_title: Set Up Firebase Analytics for Android and iOS
content.value_statement: Mobile analytics integration requires correct dependencies, configuration files, and navigation tracking. This skill guides Android and iOS setup, screen coverage planning, and event verification.
actual_capabilities: Guide Android dependency setup with Kotlin or Groovy Gradle files and variant-specific Firebase configuration.
Guide iOS dependency setup through Swift Package Manager or CocoaPods, configuration target membership, and Firebase initialization.
Create a screen inventory and track implementation progress across mobile navigation destinations.
Provide screen tracking patterns for Compose navigation, pagers, Voyager, SwiftUI views, and UIKit controllers.
Explain automatic tracking safeguards that prevent duplicate screen view events.
Guide event verification through Android Logcat, iOS debug logs, and Firebase DebugView, followed by temporary code cleanup.
limitations: Covers native Android and iOS integrations, not web analytics or cross-platform framework setup.
Requires a registered Firebase app, an Analytics-linked project, and appropriate configuration access.
Device verification requires a working mobile build environment and an emulator, simulator, or test device.
Verification instructions include agent metadata telemetry; obtain explicit approval or remove those fields before running them.

use_cases.title: Integrate Android Analytics
use_cases.description: Configure Gradle dependencies and build variants, then add Compose screen tracking and verify events on a test device.

use_cases.title: Add iOS Screen Tracking
use_cases.description: Initialize Firebase in a SwiftUI or UIKit app and add manual screen events where automatic tracking does not apply.

use_cases.title: Review Tracking Coverage
use_cases.description: Build a screen inventory, identify missing or duplicate events, and prepare a verification checklist for a mobile release.

prompt_templates.title: Understand Setup Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: List Firebase Analytics prerequisites for my Android app. Identify required project information and configuration files before suggesting edits.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a SwiftUI App
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my SwiftUI project and guide Firebase Analytics setup using Swift Package Manager. Check initialization and configuration target membership. Ask before running telemetry.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Compose Screen Tracking
prompt_templates.prompt: Inventory my Compose navigation screens and propose a tracking plan. Identify nested navigators and automatic tracking overlaps. Use stable, non-sensitive screen names.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Multi-Platform Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Android and iOS tracking coverage, configuration variants, and duplicate event risks. Propose debug verification and cleanup steps. Exclude agent metadata unless explicitly approved.

output_examples.input: Plan Firebase Analytics setup for an Android app with debug and release package identifiers.
output: Confirm that both package identifiers are registered with the intended Firebase project.
Add the Google Services plugin and Firebase Analytics dependency using compatible versions.
Place configuration files in matching variant source folders and verify the active debug package.
Verify events on a test device and remove temporary verification code.

output_examples.input: Review screen tracking coverage for a SwiftUI app with UIKit settings screens.
output: Inventory SwiftUI destinations and UIKit controllers before making edits.
Add explicit tracking to SwiftUI destinations with stable screen names.
Check automatic UIKit reporting before adding manual calls to avoid duplicate events.
Prepare DebugView checks and cleanup steps without adding unapproved agent metadata.

best_practices: Confirm Firebase project selection and app identifiers before changing configuration or transmitting test events.
Use stable, non-sensitive screen names and check automatic reporting before adding manual events.
Approve verification telemetry explicitly, use test devices, and remove temporary events and debug settings after verification.
anti_patterns: Adding manual native screen events while automatic screen reporting remains enabled.
Using configuration files that do not match the active build variant or target identifier.
Running agent metadata telemetry without approval or leaving temporary verification events in release code.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which mobile languages and interfaces are covered?
faq.answer: Android examples cover Kotlin, Java, and Compose. iOS examples cover Swift, Objective-C, SwiftUI, and UIKit.

faq.question: Does this skill create Firebase projects or handle standalone login?
faq.answer: It expects Firebase project prerequisites. It refers project creation, CLI login, and configuration downloads to the separate firebase-basics skill.

faq.question: How does it verify analytics events?
faq.answer: It describes Android Logcat, iOS debug console logs, and Firebase DebugView. Verification requires a working build and a test device or simulator.

faq.question: Does verification send agent or model information?
faq.answer: The reference workflow includes agent, model, and skill metadata in a temporary event. Remove these fields or obtain explicit approval before transmission.

faq.question: Does it configure other Firebase products?
faq.answer: No. Crashlytics, Remote Config, Authentication, Firestore, Hosting, App Hosting, and Data Connect are outside its stated scope.
